moat_basis: Annual cadence, NVFP4 formats and two-die packaging; silicon alone is now matched on paper
strongest_challenger: AMD MI455X (432 GB HBM4, 20 PFLOPS FP8 claimed); Google TPU at system level
trend_evidence: Layer 02 repo view: the silicon lead is now months, not generations; Rubin HBM4 and NVLink 6 specs cut in Sep-Oct 2026
value_capture_basis: Primary profit pool: a B200 costs ~$6.4K to build vs a $30-40K price (Est., Epoch AI)

moat_basis: Largest committed buyer and first onto each HBM generation; ~60% of 2026 CoWoS wafers (Est.)
strongest_challenger: AMD capacity-heavy HBM4 (432 vs 288 GB); HBM makers' pricing power
trend_evidence: Supply and capacity commitments rose from $119B to $279B in one quarter (Q1 to Q2 FY2027)
value_capture_basis: Pass-through cost: HBM ~45% of a B200's build cost (Est.); memory makers capture the margin
notes: Trend is NVIDIA's access advantage over rivals, not its margin on memory

moat_basis: Coherent NVLink-C2C integration and rack co-design, not better cores
strongest_challenger: AMD EPYC Venice (256 cores) as the Helios host; hyperscaler Arm CPUs
trend_evidence: Rivals out-core Vera but none matches its coherent GPU link; agentic CPU demand rising
value_capture_basis: Small: ~$180K of CPUs in a ~$7.8M Vera Rubin rack, ~2% (Est., Morgan Stanley)

moat_basis: 72-GPU NVLink domain in volume; copper spine; switch silicon, SerDes and NCCL co-designed yearly
strongest_challenger: AMD Helios (260 TB/s over UALink-on-Ethernet); Google TPU pods of 9,216 chips
trend_evidence: Helios out-specs Rubin per GPU on paper (3.6 vs 3.0 TB/s); UALink products expected 2027
value_capture_basis: High: NVLink switch trays and spine sit inside every NVL72 rack price; NVLink Fusion licences

moat_basis: Mellanox InfiniBand plus Spectrum-X Ethernet; NIC, switch and NCCL tuned and sold with the platform
strongest_challenger: Broadcom merchant Ethernet (Tomahawk 6), Arista and white-box ODMs, Ultra Ethernet
trend_evidence: Ethernet ~two-thirds of AI back-end switch sales (1Q 2026) while Spectrum-X grew 2.6x y/y
value_capture_basis: High: networking ~$31.4B in FY2026 and ~$17.5B in Q2 FY2027 (Est.), ~20% of Data Center

moat_basis: ConnectX and BlueField co-designed with DOCA, NCCL and GPUDirect
strongest_challenger: Hyperscaler offload (AWS Nitro, Google Titanium); AMD Pensando NICs (2.4 Tb/s per GPU in Helios)
trend_evidence: Rivals took ~3 years to match ConnectX at 400G but about a year or less at 800G
value_capture_basis: Medium: NICs and DPUs ~3-11% of an NVL72 rack (Est.); storage software margin goes to partners

moat_basis: One integrated rack design per year (NVLink spine, power, liquid cooling) built by an ODM ecosystem
strongest_challenger: AMD Helios (31 TB HBM4, first shipments ~end Q3 2026); Google TPU pods
trend_evidence: Helios leads Vera Rubin NVL72 on 3 of 7 rack metrics on paper
value_capture_basis: High: ~$35B of NVIDIA content in a $50-60B gigawatt; ODMs keep ~2-3%

moat_basis: Long tail: native in all 12 major frameworks (36/36), day-0 model support, ~6M developers
strongest_challenger: PyTorch/Triton/vLLM abstraction with ROCm as second backend; JAX/XLA on TPU
trend_evidence: AMD's lag on a new frontier model fell to 26 days; repo lock-in score averages ~3.6/5 but 2.75 at frontier labs
value_capture_basis: Indirect: CUDA is free and monetised through hardware margin and licences
notes: Score rounds the layer-09 segment average (data/l09_moat_by_segment.csv) to the nearest half point

moat_basis: Accumulated tuning across every GPU generation plus breadth across 15 library domains
strongest_challenger: AMD ROCm libraries (RCCL ported from NCCL); XLA and Triton compilers
trend_evidence: No rival leads in any of 15 domains and AMD matches 3; the AI core is copyable but the long tail holds
value_capture_basis: Indirect: mostly free; value shows up in GPU pricing and AI Enterprise licences

moat_basis: Serving software co-designed with rack hardware (NVL72, NVFP4) and re-tuned for each new model
strongest_challenger: Open engines (vLLM, SGLang) that also run on AMD and TPU; Google TPU on cost per token
trend_evidence: Chip specs converged but rack-scale serving has not: GB300 NVL72 ~8x MI355X per GPU at 50 tok/s/user
value_capture_basis: Low direct: software ~$2B a year, under 1% of Data Center revenue; pull-through is the point

moat_basis: Control plane acquired then opened (Run:ai, SchedMD); allocation and capital rather than licences
strongest_challenger: Hyperscalers, who own the customer, the control plane and their own chips
trend_evidence: Gap closed a lot for hyperscalers' own workloads, little for the open market
value_capture_basis: Low: rental margins sit with clouds; NVIDIA carries ~$65B of cloud commitments as a counterparty

moat_basis: Installed-base ecosystem plus ~$99B of equity stakes and deployable cash rivals cannot match
strongest_challenger: Hyperscaler plus Broadcom custom-ASIC coalition; AMD equity-for-gigawatts warrants
trend_evidence: Broadcom AI revenue rose from ~12% to ~19% of NVIDIA Data Center revenue (2024-25 to 2026-Q3)
value_capture_basis: Medium, indirect: demand creation; H1 FY2027 net equity gains of $23.7B are largely mark-to-market
notes: Capital gap widening, demand-capture gap narrowing; the layer page's competition verdict says narrowing
